title: Crypto misuse: CMAC sess_reset leaks key on wc_InitCmac failure
description: wolfssl_cmac_aes_sess_reset() in src/providers/wolfssl/wolfssl_cmac.c line 133: when wc_InitCmac() returns non-zero, the function returns wolfssl_cmac_xlat_err(ret) without calling memzero_explicit(ctx->key_bytes, sizeof(ctx->key_bytes)) or zeroing ctx->key_len. The AES key material persists in kernel memory after a failed reset. Compare to wolfssl_hmac_sess_reset() (wolfssl_hmac.c lines 198-200, 206-209) and wolfssl_aes_cbc_sess_reset() which both correctly zeroize key_bytes before returning on error. Trigger: sess_reset() called on a CMAC session where wc_InitCmac() fails (e.g. wolfCrypt internal error or FIPS degraded state). Cryptographic consequence: FIPS 140-3 key zeroization requirement (SP 800-133 §6) violated — the symmetric key remains recoverable from kernel memory after the session enters a failed state.
